messages:
anya: Quick Q  I'm flying to Berlin with a hardware prototype (small dev board + 2x 18650 packs, and a couple of power banks). Want to demo it at the offsite. Anyone shipped prototype gear before? TSA/customs rules are confusing. Do I try to carry everything on or ship to the hotel?

marc: Carry batteries in carry-on only. Spares/loose lithium cells are NOT allowed in checked baggage. For 18650s, pack them in original cells or in plastic cases and tape terminals. Power banks go in carry-on too. Airline rules vary so check the carrier page.

samira: If the battery packs are >100Wh you need airline approval. Most small 18650 packs are OK (<100Wh) but double-check math: Wh = mAh/1000 * V. Example: 3000mAh at 3.7V ~ 11.1Wh each.

anya: thanks, that math helps. What about shipping? Would shipping reduce headache or create customs pain?

noah: Shipping has pros/cons: Pros: no lugging; Cons: customs hold, lost package risk, cost. If you ship commercially, mark as "demo equipment - not for sale" and include packing list + contact phone. For EU events, ATA Carnet is overkill for a couple of boards.

marc: Pro tip: ship to the hotel with "deliver to front desk - hold for (event name)" and call hotel to confirm. Hotels sometimes charge handling fees but it's faster than customs. Also insure for declared value.

samira: Also: bring a tiny toolkit in your carry-on (hex driver, tape, cable ties). Security sometimes asks to power on devices; have a short demo script and screenshots in case you can't power it up.

anya: Good call. Any special security checks at EU airports for prototype hardware?

noah: Random checks happen. Have a one-page tech spec + serial numbers and a short note that it's a prototype for a conference. If you have any restricted crypto/comms features, check export controls first.

marc: If demo uses an LTE modem/antenna, that's more likely to trigger customs. Remove SIMs or disable radios. Also bring a battery meter or label showing Wh to speed up staff who ask.

cargo-bot: NOTE: Airline policy reminder - spare lithium batteries must be in carry-on and terminals taped. Check airline carry-on battery limit: some carriers cap to 160Wh without approval.

samira: If you decide to check a hard case (not batteries), use a hard-shell case and declare fragile. But again, batteries stay with you.

anya: Logistics question: anyone willing to help carry demo to the demo table if I need a hand setting up? I might be juggling bags + kid stuff. React with "I'll help" or DM me.

marc: I'll help setup. Also bring an HDMI adapter and a short USB-C cable  hotels rarely have the right lead.

noah: And bring an EU plug adapter, power strip with safe surge (but don't plug big batteries into hotel power directly), and a small UPS only if rated for travel.

samira: Final checklist I use: 1) docs & photos of gear, 2) batteries in carry-on + taped terminals, 3) toolkit, 4) printed demo script, 5) shipping label pre-made as backup. Save this thread.

anya: This is perfect  thank you. Saved checklist. DMing @marc to coordinate pickup. :heart:

cargo-bot: Reminder: If shipping from US to EU, declare value accurately. Customs may charge VAT on high-value items.
